zarr backend of the store layer (writing)

Source: R/io-store-zarr-write.R
io-store-zarr-write.Rd

The write operations of io-store for a local zarr v3 directory store.

Usage

zarr_create(path)

zarr_encode_values(values, dtype)

zarr_vlen_encode(values)

zarr_zstd(payload)

zarr_consolidate(path)

Arguments

path

Path of the store directory.

values

The values of an array, in R's order.

dtype

A dtype name: numeric_dtypes, "bool", "complex128" or "string".

payload

A raw vector of encoded chunk bytes.

Details

Rarr writes the chunks of numeric and bool arrays (compressed with zstd, the codec Python uses), and the metadata (zarr.json) is always written by us so that it matches what Python writes (the On-disk dtype given explicitly, no identity transpose codec, the fill value and codecs of Python). What Rarr cannot write is done here, following ADR 0007:

  • 0-d arrays (scalars and null) and variable-length UTF-8 strings: the chunk bytes are encoded in R and compressed by Rarr (as a uint8 array, whose single chunk is exactly the compressed bytes)

  • 64-bit integers from doubles, the int32 minimum and uint32 values beyond the R integer range, and complex values: the bytes of each value are split into 16-bit (or float64) parts along a trailing dimension that Rarr writes, and the chunk keys then lose that dimension, which is the inverse of zarr_split_read()

The compressors dataset argument chooses the compressor (zstd by default, see zarr_compressor_arg()), and nothing is sharded yet.
